mission: Cockpit. Desh converts the seal degradation rate into hours and posts the countdown on the bulkhead in a number small enough to memorise. Nobody wants to. Ben paces the common area assigning approach tasks. Torin appears in the doorway: 'We need to talk about what happens when we get there.' His voice is calm and warm and decided.
why_now: The timeline collapsed at the end of Ch16 and has to be physicalised into an on-ship countdown before the chapter can move. Torin's doorway line can only land now — earlier would have been premature, later would have been a surprise Ben has earned the right to see coming.
conflict: The pressure intensifies every friction. The wound's amplification is working on the group by proximity. Ben assigns tasks and tries to hear the ship sound normal. Torin steps into the frame with a sentence that is not a question.
turning_point: Torin's tone. Ben has heard the cadence before. Jacen used it in the weeks before the worst things happened — the warmth of someone who has already decided and is negotiating the announcement.
opening_hook: Desh converts the seal degradation rate to hours and posts the number on the cockpit display. It's small enough to memorize. Nobody wants to.
closing_hook: Torin's tone. Ben has heard that tone before. Jacen used it in the weeks before the worst things happened — the certainty of someone who has already decided and is now only negotiating the announcement.
emotional_trajectory: Urgent tactical focus -> group pressure cracking -> Torin's ominous calm

stakes.personal: Ben hearing the Jacen pattern in Torin's voice — the recognition crystallising
stakes.interpersonal: Torin separating from the group emotionally even while physically present

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit and common area, hyperspace toward Veranthos
sensory_details: Desh's countdown numeral on the bulkhead, steady against Ben's pulse; the wrongness a constant pressure like altitude sickness sitting at the back of the head; arguments flaring hotter than their content justifies; Torin's silhouette in the doorway carrying the exact weight of an old remembered cadence
action_beats: Desh converts the seal degradation rate to hours and posts the countdown on the cockpit display
Ben paces the common area while assigning approach tasks — nerves converting to motion
Torin stands in the doorway and speaks with the calm warm tone that drops Ben's stomach
notes: H17 planted. The most ominous hook in the book because it is delivered with warmth — do not have Torin's line sound like a threat; do not have Ben on-page articulate 'that is how Jacen talked.' The reader hears it through the doorway cadence; Ben's interior register the drop without naming the analogy. Torin's arc deepens — the certainty is now a decision. Anti-pattern: Torin's actual argument is not delivered here; the line is the hook for Ch21, and the chapter must not pay it off early.
